title: Stochastic dominance of first return times for nearest-neighbor random walks on $\mathbb{Z}^d$
summary: For a $d$-dimensional probability vector $\mathbf{h}=(h_1,\dots, h_d)$, let $(S^{\mathbf{h}}_n)_{n\geq 0}$ be a nearest-neighbor random walk on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ such that at each step, it moves to one of the two nearest neighbors in the $i$-th dimension with probability $\frac{1}{2} h_i$ ($i=1,\dots, d$). Let $T^{\mathbf{h}}=\inf\{n\geq 1: S^{\mathbf{h}}_n=(0,\dots,0)\}$, the first return time to the origin.
